inspection: Read the unstaged diff and nearby bootstrap, setup, configuration, and test context.
git diff --check for the two target files exited 0.
No tests were run, as directed; ROOT-reported green results were not independently reproduced.
Reviewed Git show-ref and worktree command semantics against the official Git documentation.

intended_outcome: After a failed git worktree add -b, remove only the branch and worktree proven to belong to that exact attempt; preserve pre-existing or unrelated state; use exact-target Git cleanup; report incomplete recovery; retain public error codes and normal successful behavior.

findings.title: The preflight absence check does not prove that post-failure state was created by this attempt.
evidence: The path and ref are observed before the add at bootstrap.py:141-153, then git worktree add -b is invoked later at :155-163.
On any nonzero add result, :169-172 invokes destructive rollback solely because the earlier ref probe returned 1.
Rollback removes the named path at :95-97 and deletes any subsequently existing refs/heads/<branch> at :102-107; neither action verifies an attempt-owned Git identity.

A concurrent actor can create the branch or register a worktree after the preflight and before the failed add. The add then fails because that state exists, and this code deletes the unrelated branch or worktree. Git's documented -b behavior refusing an existing branch makes this interleaving directly relevant.
findings.consequence: This violates the core safety condition. A failed bootstrap can force-delete another actor's unmerged branch and remove that actor's exact-path worktree, rather than only recovering the Windows long-path attempt.
findings.smallest_useful_correction: Acquire and record branch/worktree ownership atomically before any destructive recovery, then condition deletion on the recorded identity still matching. If an exact-attempt proof cannot be established, fail closed and report incomplete rollback rather than remove the ref or path. Verify the target worktree through Git metadata before removing it.

findings.title: Rollback performs a repository-wide worktree prune, not only exact-target cleanup.
evidence: After the exact-path worktree remove, bootstrap.py:98 runs git worktree prune without a path or ownership filter.
Git documents worktree prune as pruning worktree information in the repository's entire $GIT_DIR/worktrees area, so it can remove stale administrative entries belonging to other worktrees.
findings.consequence: A single failed lane can mutate unrelated worktree metadata, including records intentionally retained for a temporarily unavailable worktree. That exceeds the requested exact-target recovery scope even though it avoids a broad filesystem deletion.
findings.smallest_useful_correction: Do not run global prune in this rollback path. Use git worktree remove --force only for a Git-verified attempt-owned target; if residual metadata cannot be safely removed by an exact-target operation, retain it and report rollback as incomplete.

findings.title: Managed materialization rejects a valid, already-materialized ROOT hook binding.
evidence: replace_if_matches accepts a worker overwrite only when the target bytes equal the raw root-catalog file at bootstrap.py:212-219; the map is built from raw root payload files at :404-409.

setup.py:548-584 explicitly supports a ROOT binding that has been materialized with the exact harness_root and runtime_root. Such a valid tracked binding copied into a worktree differs from the raw root template and also differs from the worker binding, so bootstrap.py:210-221 raises BOOTSTRAP_CACHE_COLLISION.
The new replacement test at test_v2_materialization.py:953-994 uses a raw root byte string, while the config test at :886-950 covers config and hooks but not an accepted materialized binding.
findings.consequence: A supported product configuration can make a normal managed bootstrap fail during overlay materialization, despite unchanged public success behavior being required.
findings.smallest_useful_correction: Recognize the valid materialized ROOT binding through the same setup validation/materialization contract before allowing the worker payload replacement; continue rejecting foreign or user-modified bindings. Add a regression using a base worktree containing the valid materialized binding.

findings.title: An exception while starting a rollback Git command loses the required incomplete-rollback report.
evidence: _run_git directly calls subprocess.run without converting OSError at bootstrap.py:72-81.

The immediate failure path calls _rollback_bootstrap_worktree without a protective catch at :169-172, so a rollback-launch exception bypasses the constructed rollback_suffix and original add error at :174-181.
run_bootstrap then treats the worktree as not created and returns the raw generic exception because rollback_failure_summary exits at :558-560, rather than reporting incomplete rollback.
findings.consequence: A recovery failure such as a later Git executable or process-launch error can conceal both the failed add and the fact that cleanup was not completed.
findings.smallest_useful_correction: Catch rollback invocation exceptions inside _git_worktree_add, preserve the original add diagnostic, and append an explicit rollback incomplete diagnostic. Cover that exception path in the focused tests.

contract_coverage.criterion: Remove only a branch proven absent before and created by the exact failed attempt
contract_coverage.evidence: bootstrap.py:145-172 proves only an earlier absence, not exact-attempt creation; F-001.

An initially existing ref skips the rollback branch deletion at bootstrap.py:153 and :169-172, and test_v2_materialization.py:65-82 covers that narrow case. A ref created after the probe is still deleted; F-001.

contract_coverage.criterion: Use ordinary exact-target Git worktree cleanup without affecting unrelated worktrees
contract_coverage.evidence: The remove command is exact-path at bootstrap.py:95-97, but the unscoped prune at :98 expands the operation to all stale worktree metadata; F-002.

Nonzero prune, failed branch deletion, surviving branch, and surviving path create notes at bootstrap.py:99-131. A rollback subprocess exception escapes the immediate path without the required report; F-004.

contract_coverage.criterion: Preserve existing public error codes and normal successful behavior
contract_coverage.evidence: The failure code remains BOOTSTRAP_REQUEST_INVALID at bootstrap.py:179-181 and the success result remains BOOTSTRAP_OK at :697-705, but a supported managed configuration regresses to BOOTSTRAP_CACHE_COLLISION; F-003.

contract_coverage.criterion: Use Git return codes and branch names safely
contract_coverage.evidence: show-ref's ordinary 0-present and 1-missing semantics are handled at bootstrap.py:148-153, and branch deletion uses -- at :107. Those correct argument/return-code details do not supply the missing ownership proof in F-001.

optional_improvements.improvement: Include the Git return code in rollback diagnostics and use Git's porcelain worktree listing for post-cleanup evidence instead of relying only on Path.exists().

verification_gaps: The mocked failure test at test_v2_materialization.py:20-63 does not model a branch or worktree appearing after the preflight, and it does not assert the exact remove/prune command sequence or state transition proving ownership.
No focused test asserts the returned public code and rollback incomplete summary for prune failure, branch-delete failure, surviving target path, or a subprocess exception during immediate rollback.
No test exercises the motivating real Git checkout failure on Windows long paths, nor an actual Git worktree cleanup record; the review did not run tests by instruction.
No test places a setup-accepted materialized ROOT binding in the base worktree before managed bootstrap, leaving F-003 unguarded.
